title: Brahmagupta's Formula for Cyclic Quadrilaterals
description: Brahmagupta's formula: Area = √((s-a)(s-b)(s-c)(s-d)) for cyclic quadrilaterals. Proves algebraic identities, reduction to Heron, positivity, concrete examples, and the key factored form.

meta.author: Brahmagupta (628 CE)
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms (Ptolemy's theorem, area via diagonals — geometric placeholders). 0 sorries.
originalContributions: Brahmagupta product expansion and factored forms

overview.historicalContext: Brahmagupta (628 CE) generalized Heron's formula to cyclic quadrilaterals in his Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta. The formula gives the area in terms of the four sides and the semi-perimeter.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize Brahmagupta's formula for cyclic quadrilaterals.
overview.text: Defines the Brahmagupta product, proves algebraic identities, shows reduction to Heron, and verifies concrete examples.
overview.proofStrategy: All algebraic identities proved by ring. Positivity from quadrilateral inequality. Concrete examples by norm_num + sqrt_sq.
keyInsights: Setting d=0 recovers Heron: product becomes s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)
The factored form ((a+b)²-(c-d)²)((c+d)²-(a-b)²) is useful for inequalities

conclusion.summary: Brahmagupta's formula formalized with algebraic identities, reduction to Heron, and concrete examples. Full geometric proof (via Ptolemy) remains for future work.
